title: Declare the runtime the file executes in

facts.note: Every non-test implementation file, whether newly created or already existing, and regardless of whether its header is edited in the current change. Test files are excluded by the source.
No layer restriction: the obligation applies across all layers of the Bun stack (server and browser alike).

values: <files belonging to a project whose stack is Bun>
facts.note: Stack context must be explicit (repository stack configuration identifying the Bun realization). Language (TypeScript/JavaScript) is NOT a proxy, since the Vite stack uses the same languages with a different vocabulary. Needs an observer that resolves the file's stack from repository configuration.

Whether the declared value matches the file's actual server/browser execution path (including genuine dual execution) needs an observer that traces the module's real runtime; the detector checks presence/vocabulary. Findings are repair triggers, not prerequisites for the obligation.

fires: A new implementation file in a Bun-stack project has no `Runtime:` header line.
An existing implementation file in a Bun-stack project lacks a `Runtime:` line, even if the current change does not touch its header.
An implementation file's `Runtime:` value is not one of `bun`, `browser`, `isomorphic`.
An implementation file's declared runtime does not match where it actually executes (e.g. its execution path changed but the header was left untouched).
A module runs both server-side and again in the browser and is declared with a single-side value instead of `isomorphic`.
doesNotFire: Files in Vite or Python stacks (handled by their own per-stack detectors with their own vocabulary).

given: A non-test implementation file in a Bun-stack project, new or existing
when: the file is present in the codebase (created, edited, or untouched) and its runtime declaration is checked
then: The file MUST carry a `Runtime:` declaration naming where it actually executes: `bun`, `browser`, or `isomorphic`.
prefer: During GREEN: derive the value from the real execution path created or used by the current acceptance (where the module is actually loaded and run), not from file location or hypothetical reuse.
During GREEN: keep an existing correct runtime declaration.
During GREEN: change only the header when the implementation already executes in the correct place.
Use `isomorphic` only for a module that genuinely runs both server-side and in the browser.
avoid: Broadening the fix: moving code between server and browser merely to fit a preferred label.
Guessing `isomorphic` because the file could theoretically run in both places.
Picking a wrong single-side value for a module that really runs in both places.
why: Bun decides at run time what a bundler decides at build time, so a full-stack Bun module can routinely run in both places; without an `isomorphic` value authors would be forced to pick a wrong one and every downstream reader would inherit the error.
evidence: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-HEADER-001 / BUN-GREEN-HEADER-RUNTIME-001 finding for the file (findings are evidence/repair triggers, not activation prerequisites).
The declaration matches where the file actually executes (a valid value alone is not sufficient).
The current behavioral acceptance passes in its real runtime.
verifier_detail: Runtime field = the `Runtime:` header line naming where the file executes; allowed values on Bun: `bun`, `browser`, `isomorphic`.
A missing declaration is reported at the URN line, or at the first meaningful line when there is no URN.
Test files are excluded from detection.
Per-stack vocabulary: Vite reads `vite|browser|node`, Python reads `python`; `isomorphic` has no Vite counterpart and is the substantive Bun addition.

Rationale for isomorphic: a bundler stack decides at BUILD time which code reaches the browser, so a file is server or client by where the bundler puts it; Bun decides at RUN time, e.g. a fragment renderer used server-side and again after a client-side swap.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Aliases: GREEN-HEADER-001 (shared core alias, also carried by the Python realization and coder.vite.green-header-runtime — one obligation, three per-stack detectors), BUN-GREEN-HEADER-RUNTIME-001.
Stack-neutral obligation ("the file says where it runs"), Bun-specific vocabulary; realized by bun_green_traceability_detector (core alias GREEN-HEADER-001).

sharedNodes.text: strict: the stack's checker fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
